title: Piano technique: front off, pedals and left hand
summary: He says taking the piano front off was unnecessary, describes paper behind strings for a drum sound, no pedals, and short versus swinging bass.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: When you played those house parties, did you usually take the front off the piano? I know that baby Bruce had the front and the top off his piano. Was that the usual thing?

No, no. That wasn't necessary. I'd say, Plenty of people, they'd do it to make the sound come out. I'll tell you another thing they used to do. To make the piano sound like a drum. You could hear the piano and the drum. They'd get a big piece of paper, and they'd put behind them the strings, behind the keys. They'd been hit on them. You had a tap on the paper from the keys, and you had the string playing the music. Plenty of people do that. A lot of them would open the front of the piano there, and they'd take that front off there and throw it back. But that was unnecessary. If you could play, you could play.
Yeah, you'd always make the sound come out. The best thing about it is to get there and sit down and play. And know what you was doing. That's all I said about it.
Yeah, did you use the pedals much on the piano?

No, I didn't have to bother with the pedal on the piano. I don't bother with that too much. You need to, uh, if you got on a good piano, if you got on a good piano, you had, you had all you wanted there. With all them keys they had in front of you. You had all you wanted with all them keys they had in front of you, you got on a good piano. That's all I said.
Did you use a lot of left hand, a lot of bass? Big Bruce said he was known for using his left hand quite a bit.

Oh, yeah, I could do it. Keep his left hand, his left hand. Yeah, well, you see, but you could take and, you could take and just sit there and play the blues and different things, short hand. Just play them right in the short. Then another time, you just take long, you lose long basses. Oh, yeah. And just use them swinging basses. Well, that's most of the time when you go into jazzing. When you're going to really jazz out of peace, you take and you use that long bass. And if you just could play it long, slow, and play the bottom of the play, well, you just go along and play. You didn't have to take and use some swinging basses in there. You didn't have to use a swing bass. Once you use a swing bass is when you would be jazzing a piece. You watch most of the piano players a day, how to do it. If they're not going to take and jazz a piece, you see how they play in short. And they take and, when they go to jazz and you see that hand, that hand will get a whip and whether they want it or not, that hand is going. Yeah, they know right where it's going. And after you play that piece, you can turn all around and be looking and talking to everybody. That hand is going to go in the right place. It ain't going to go in the wrong place. You don't have to see it. The eagle's apple is going to the right place where it belongs. And that's amazing.
